A practical implementation is a masked, normalized recurrence: train scalar or per-channel retention `a = sigmoid(theta)`; initialize `s=z=0`; at each valid position compute `s=a*s+x`, `z=a*z+1`, and `h=s/z`. Padding preserves both states and emits zero. Accumulate in float32 under mixed precision; preserve float64 for numerical tests. This formulation avoids inverse powers and division by `1-a`: near zero it selects the latest item; near one it approaches the prefix mean. Use explicitly masked item embeddings before adding positional information. These are implementation recommendations derived from the recurrence.

For short SASRec sequences, start with a batched PyTorch loop, optionally compiled. For greater parallelism, represent each step as an affine map `(A,B)`, composing chronological maps as `(A2*A1, A2*B1+B2)`; padding is the identity `(1,0)`. Apply this to both numerator and denominator. An ordinary tensor doubling scan provides logarithmic depth with autograd, although memory traffic can outweigh benefits at short lengths. PyTorch’s [associative scan documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/higher_order_ops/associative_scan.html) describes parallel tree execution but marks the API experimental; verify gradients and compiler behavior on the installed version. Fuse each prefix output into its matching SASRec feature and supervise every valid position against its next-item target.

Verify against an explicit float64 weighted-prefix reference, including extreme retentions and all-padding inputs. Run [gradcheck](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.autograd.gradcheck.gradcheck.html) on embeddings and decay logits; check finite gradients near both endpoints. Perturb suffixes and compare unchanged earlier outputs; compare full-sequence outputs with separately evaluated prefixes. Prepend padding and compare aligned valid outputs, using padding-independent positions. Finally, reload each category’s checkpoint through the generated predictor in evaluation mode and compare features, candidate scores, and rankings with the training model. Persist architecture settings, decay parameters, routing, and positional conventions.
